about.title: Selma Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Selma's population of roughly 24,414 relies heavily on a handful of busy corridors — Floral Avenue, Highland Avenue, Mccall Avenue, and Golden State Boulevard — to move through town and connect to nearby farmland and packing routes. Public records show 41 injury collisions in the most recent final year, with 60 people injured, and reports tend to cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., likely tied to end-of-week traffic and shift changes. After a crash on any of these roads, decisions made in the first days matter: photos fade, skid marks get repaved, and witnesses move on. Our team helps injured Selma residents gather evidence, deal with insurance adjusters, and evaluate a claim — all before a critical deadline passes. There's no cost for a case review, and no obligation to move forward.

items.title: You Don't Face the Clock Alone
items.desc: California generally allows two years to file a car accident claim, but that window shrinks dramatically — sometimes to six months — if a government entity, like a county road agency, is involved. We can quickly identify which deadline applies to your Selma crash.

items.title: Fault-Sharing Won't Erase Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for what happened on Highland Avenue or Golden State Boulevard. We can help make sure any shared-fault argument from the insurer doesn't unfairly shrink your claim.

items.title: Avoid the Recorded Statement Trap
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement early, hoping to lock in details that limit your claim later. Our team can speak for you instead, helping preserve evidence and protect your right to full non-economic damages, which California does not cap.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Selma?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity — such as a city or county road department — may be responsible, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Because of this, it's smart to get a claim reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some blame for the collision. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated entirely. We can help push back if an insurer tries to inflate your share of responsibility.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since adjusters may use your words to minimize your claim later. This is especially relevant in Selma, where crashes reported along corridors like Mccall Avenue or Golden State Boulevard often involve quick insurer outreach. Our team can communicate with the insurer on your behalf instead.

items.question: Does this service charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No — there is no charge for a free case review. Our team works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
